items.title: Government opens toll roads: "Call it system change"
items.summary: Some new motorways may in the future be paid for directly by those who use them. With two new decisions, the government opens up more ways to plan for infrastructure where a state company is allowed to compete with the Swedish Transport Administration. - Feel free to call it a system change, much like both Denmark and Norway did a long time ago, says Minister Andreas Carlson (KD).
items.title_original: Regeringen öppnar för betalvägar: ”Kalla det gärna systemskifte”
items.summary_original: Vissa nya bilvägar kan i framtiden betalas direkt av dem som använder dem. Med två nya beslut öppnar regeringen för fler sätt att planera för infrastruktur där ett statligt bolag får konkurrera med Trafikverket. – Kalla det gärna ett systemskifte, ungefär som både Danmark och Norge gjort för länge sedan, säger ministern Andreas Carlson (KD).

items.title: The state can take over responsibility for forensic psychiatry
items.summary: Forensic psychiatry has long been overcrowded, which has led, among other things, to convicts being released while waiting for a place. An investigation is now being added into how the state can fully or partially take over responsibility for care. - We are preparing for the biggest reform ever in forensic psychiatry, says Minister of Social Affairs Jakob Forssmed (KD).
items.title_original: Staten kan ta över ansvar för rättspsykiatrin
items.summary_original: Rättspsykiatrin har länge varit överfull, vilket bland annat lett till att dömda släppts ut i väntan på en plats. Nu tillsätts en utredning om hur staten helt eller delvis kan ta över ansvaret för vården. – Vi förbereder för den största reformen någonsin i rättspsykiatrin, säger socialminister Jakob Forssmed (KD).

items.title: Record heat in Western Europe in June
items.summary: Last month's heatwave produced the hottest June on record in Western Europe, according to Copernicus, the EU's environmental monitoring satellite system.
items.title_original: Rekordvärme i Västeuropa i juni
items.summary_original: Värmeböljan förra månaden gav den varmaste junimånaden hittills i Västeuropa, enligt Copernicus, EU:s satellitsystem för miljöövervakning.

items.title: EU adopts sanctions over poisoning of Russian opposition politician Alexei Navalny
items.summary: In light of the poisoning of Alexei Navalny, the EU has adopted sanctions against six Russian individuals under the chemical weapons sanctions regime. In June, listings of seven individuals and one entity were also adopted under the EU Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime, which was established because of the internal oppression in Russia.

items.title: Government invests SEK 250 million in global health
items.summary: The Government has adopted a new support package for global health, including sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), totalling SEK 250 million for 2026. The health package consolidates Sweden’s commitment to improving the health of the most vulnerable through vaccines in low- and middle-income countries and increased access to maternal and newborn care where the needs are greatest.

items.title: The ESRB warns of vulnerabilities in the financial system linked to advanced AI models
items.summary: The European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB), the EU's macro-supervisory body, issues a formal warning about vulnerabilities in the financial system linked to advanced AI models. The ESRB's warning calls on relevant authorities to take such risks into account in supervision and monitoring.
items.title_original: ESRB varnar för sårbarheter i det finansiella systemet kopplade till avancerade AI-modeller
items.summary_original: Europeiska systemrisknämnden (ESRB), EU:s makrotillsynsorgan, utfärdar en formell varning om sårbarheter i det finansiella systemet, kopplade till avancerade AI-modeller. ESRB:s varning uppmanar relevanta myndigheter att ta hänsyn till sådana risker i tillsyn och övervakning.

items.title: NATO selects Saab GlobalEye Airborne Warning and Control System
items.summary: Today, 7 July, in connection with the NATO Summit in Ankara, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte announced that NATO has chosen Saab’s GlobalEye as its new Airborne Early Warning & Control (AEW&C). This means that NATO will open negotiations with Saab to purchase up to 10 GlobalEye aircraft.

items.title: From Kiev to Kyjiv – Sweden changes Embassy name
items.summary: On 2 July 2026, Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard announced that the Swedish names of the Embassy of Sweden in Kyiv and the Honorary Consulate of Sweden in Odesa will be changed to reflect the Ukrainian names for Kyiv and Odesa, respectively.

items.title: Poland procures three A26 submarines from Saab following talks with Swedish Government
items.summary: On 29 June, Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson visited Gdynia, Poland for government-level talks. The meeting focused on strengthened bilateral cooperation between Sweden and Poland in the areas of regional security and defence. Minister for Defence Pål Jonson, Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard, Minister for Culture Parisa Liljestrand, Minister for Infrastructure and Housing Andreas Carlson and Minister for EU Affairs Jessica Rosencrantz also took part on the trip.

items.title: Sweden provides SEK 25 million to earthquake-stricken Venezuela
items.summary: The two earthquakes in Venezuela on 24 June have had a profound impact on the Venezuelan people and exacerbated an already difficult humanitarian situation. Sweden is now providing SEK 25 million in humanitarian assistance to Venezuela to support initiatives such as the distribution of food packages, access to clean water, temporary emergency shelter, protection of vulnerable groups and reunification of children and families who have been separated.

items.title: Government overhauls development assistance to Africa, Latin America and Asia
items.summary: The Government has adopted nine new development assistance strategies which will provide a total of around SEK 6 billion for development cooperation in Africa, Latin America and Asia. The new development assistance will be based on evidence of what works and produces concrete results.

items.title: Offline card payments - now the possibilities are expanding
items.summary: As of today, July 1, 2026, expanded opportunities to pay by card offline will be introduced when purchasing essential goods. The measure strengthens the resilience of the payment system and is based on an agreement between the Riksbank and market participants.
items.title_original: Offlinebetalningar med kort - nu utökas möjligheterna
items.summary_original: Från och med i dag, 1 juli 2026, införs utökade möjligheter att betala med kort offline vid köp av livsnödvändiga varor. Åtgärden stärker betalningssystemets motståndskraft och bygger på en överenskommelse mellan Riksbanken och marknadsaktörer.

items.title: Poland signs agreement to procure submarines from Saab and deepen strategic cooperation with Sweden
items.summary: Sweden and Poland have successfully finalised negotiations on Poland’s procurement of three A26 submarines from Saab. This agreement is a significant step in strengthening Poland’s maritime capability, while also helping the countries deepen their collaboration on security and industrial policy.

items.summary: Concluding the first Polish-Swedish Intergovernmental Consultations on 29 June 2026, in Gdynia, Poland and Sweden agreed to deepen their bilateral security and defence cooperation in the Baltic Sea region by launching the Baltic Sea Pact.

items.title: Joint Declaration from the Polish-Swedish Intergovernmental Consultations Gdynia
items.summary: The Republic of Poland and the Kingdom of Sweden are close Baltic Sea neighbours, Allies and partners, tied together by shared history, geography and responsibility for their strategically important region. Our Governments meet on 29 June 2026 for the first time in the format of Intergovernmental Consultations, a year and a half after the signing of the renewed Strategic Partnership between Poland and Sweden (Harpsund, 28 November 2024).

items.title: Sweden takes next major step towards new nuclear power
items.summary: The Government has decided that the state will become a shareholder in Videberg Kraft AB, which plans to build nuclear reactors at Ringhals. The Swedish state, Vattenfall AB and Industrikraft i Sverige AB have concluded a shareholders’ agreement on the management of the company. The state’s shareholding will be 60 per cent, while Vattenfall and Industrikraft will each hold 20 per cent. The state has also negotiated the principal terms and conditions for state aid to the company.

items.title: Sweden strengthens Ukraine’s energy supply ahead of winter
items.summary: Last winter, Ukraine’s electrical grid and power plants were intensively attacked by Russia. Ukraine must now make extensive efforts to ensure the energy supply for the coming winter. The Swedish Government has therefore approved a new support package for Ukraine worth approximately SEK 1.5 billion to support the country’s energy sector in 2026. It is expected to contribute to preparation through repairs, installation of new energy production, material support and enhanced nuclear safety.
